sector_model: IT and AI data services: customer concentration, gross margin, working capital and customer prepayments, SBC
thesis: Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD), AI data engineering and annotation services. Q3 2026 10-Q (0001104659-26-123437, filed 2026-11-05) and release Ex99.1 (8-K 0001104659-26-123324). Q3 revenue 95.6M (+53%), net income 10.3M (diluted EPS 0.29), adjusted EBITDA 17.7M (18.5%), GAAP gross margin 37%. 2026 revenue growth guide raised to about 42% or more. A customer under 5% of revenue a year ago became the largest in Q3 (percentage undisclosed). TTM (XBRL: FY2025 + 9M26 - 9M25): revenue 350.2M, net income 48.5M, OCF 93.5M (Q3 alone -84.0M after H1 164.4M), capex 10.5M, FCF 83.0M, 9M SBC 19.9M. Cash 164.0M at 2026-09-30 (240.3M at 2026-06-30), about 153.7M net of customer prepayments; long term obligations 11.3M; liabilities 93.1M; equity 176.5M. Shares 34.41M (10-Q cover 2026-10-30), market cap about 1.22B at 35.46: TTM P/E 25.1x, FCF yield 6.8% but inflated by customer prepayments that reversed in Q3, EV about 1.07B. Market view: a small AI services winner whose price assumes the new top customer stays; evidence for: growth, net cash, profits; gap closing needs revenue per customer visibility.
counterthesis: Revenue growth rests on a few large technology customers whose spending is lumpy and can move to in-house or competing labeling vendors (Scale-type firms, offshore vendors); the new largest customer was under 5% a year ago, which shows how fast concentration shifts. Q3 operating cash flow was about -84M, so trailing FCF of 83M reflects prepayment timing, not steady earnings power. SBC of about 20M over nine months is 7% of revenue and dilutes (diluted shares 35.6M versus 34.4M outstanding). Net income grew only 24% on 53% revenue growth, so margins are compressing (gross margin 37%). Small cap with a history of sharp swings (35 to 38 in a week). 10-Q text, MD&A, customer concentration note and peers were not read.
invalidation: Thesis fails if the largest customer cuts volume, revenue per quarter stalls, gross margin falls further, operating cash flow stays negative after prepayments, or dilution accelerates.
